neet_phy_u12_t02_1.working: Ohm's law holds for a metal wire only at constant temperature. In that case V ∝ I, so the graph is a straight line through the origin. A diode, a filament lamp and a voltameter are all non-linear.

neet_phy_u12_t02_2.working: With V on the y-axis and I on the x-axis, R equals the slope. So R = tan60° = √3 Ω.

neet_phy_u12_t02_3.working: The slope of an I-V graph is 1/R. This gives R1 = 1/0.5 = 2 Ω and R2 = 1/0.25 = 4 Ω. A metal's resistance rises with temperature, so T2 > T1, and R at T2 is 4 Ω.

neet_phy_u12_t02_4.working: Passing through the origin does not make a device ohmic. A filament bulb's resistance rises as it heats, so its V-I graph is non-linear and it is non-ohmic. Hence A is false and R is true.

neet_phy_u12_t02_5.working: For a non-ohmic device, dV/dI is generally not equal to V/I, so I is false. GaAs has a negative-resistance region where the same current occurs at more than one voltage, so II is true.
